newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise slightly, rate worries loom.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise slightly, rate worries loom.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly higher late Friday, following small gains in U.S. Treasuries.

Traders said despite the release of market friendly U.S. indicators Friday, U.S. bonds and thereby the Argentine market were hampered by continued concerns that the Federal Reserve will raise rates on March 25. "People are concerned. We will continue to see high volatility in the short-term," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior analyst at Banco Rio.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.09 to 126.29.
Another analyst said the market's mood has changed a little over the last couple of sessions as local players have become more aware of the potential of a rate hike in the United States.
Those concerns are set to dominate market activity next week, until the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25, said traders.
"The market is looking closely at the U.S. long bond," added Bourdieu.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.98 percent from 6.13 percent.
